top_news.title: Malta Tourism Authority and Trip.com Group Sign Strategic Cooperation Memorandum of Understanding to Promote Malta as a Global Destination
top_news.summary: VALLETTA, Malta, Oct. 13, 2026 /PRNewswire/ -- On the sidelines of the 2026 WTTC Global Summit held in Malta, Carlo Micallef, CEO of the Malta Tourism Authority, met with Edison Chen, Vice President of Trip.com Group, for talks on China-Malta tourism cooperation. Witnessed by Jo Etienne Abela, Malta's Minister for Tourism, the Malta Tourism Authority and Trip.com Group formally signed the 2026-2029 Strategic Cooperation Memorandum of Understanding. Malta Tourism Authority and Trip.com Group sign a Strategic Cooperation Memorandum of Understanding to promote Malta as a global destination over the next three years. DOI (Malta) The signing of the Strategic Cooperation MOU marks a further deepening of the strategic partnership between the Malta Tourism Authority and Trip.com Group. Over the next three years, the two parties will carry out in-depth cooperation in destination promotion, tourism product diversification and sustainable tourism. (From left to right) Carlo Micallef, CEO of the Malta Tourism Authority, together with Jo Etienne Abela, Malta's Minister for Tourism, met with Edison Chen, Vice President of Trip.com Group, for talks on China-Malta tourism cooperation. Trip.com Group "Malta is committed to diversifying its source markets, and China is the most important emerging market in our strategic plans," said CarloMicallef, CEO of the Malta Tourism Authority. "Our partnership with Trip.com Group will help us reach high-value travellers in China and around the world more precisely, and showcase Malta's unique appeal as a premium Mediterranean tourism destination." Edison Chen, Vice President of Trip.com Group, said, "Malta is a vibrant destination, offering a wealth of cultural and premium experiences, and excellent connectivity. Our data shows a 60% growth in inbound travel bookings to Malta, underscoring its growing appeal among global travellers. By combining Trip.com Group's global reach and platform technology with Malta's unique offerings, we are excited to further boost tourism in Malta, inspiring more travellers from Asia and around the world to discover its beauty." Malta Accelerates Its Push into the Asian Market Malta is actively expanding into the Asian market, with plans to raise the share of arrivals from outside the EU to 40% within the next decade. Carlo Micallef, CEO of the Malta Tourism Authority, said that Malta is advancing tourism cooperation discussions with China and several other Asian countries. Although Schengen visa requirements remain a short-term challenge, the market potential is immense. Trip.com Group's platform coverage advantages across the world's major source markets, together with its leading big-data and AI-supported capabilities, will help Malta enhance its brand influence as a premium tourism destination. With a large presence in Asia, Europe and across global markets, Trip.com Group is highly strategically aligned with the Malta Tourism Authority's market diversification strategy. The 2026 WTTC Global Summit was held from 7 to 9 October at the Mediterranean Conference Centre in Valletta, bringing together tourism industry CEOs and senior government leaders from more than 100 countries. The signing is one of the significant cooperation outcomes achieved during the Summit. Over the next three years, the two parties will leverage the technological capabilities and data insights of Trip.com Group's global platforms, combined with the Malta Tourism Authority's in-depth understanding and integration of local tourism resources, to continuously optimise promotional strategies and position Malta as a highly attractive Mediterranean tourism destination for global travellers. About Trip.com Group Trip.com Group is a global travel service provider comprising of Trip.com, Ctrip, Skyscanner, and Qunar. Across its platforms, Trip.com Group helps travellers around the world make informed and cost-effective bookings for travel products and services and enables partners to connect their offerings with users through the aggregation of travel-related content and resources, and an advanced transaction platform consisting of apps, websites and 24/7 customer service centres. Founded in 1999 and listed on NASDAQ in 2003 and HKEX in 2021, Trip.com Group is on the mission "to pursue the perfect trip for a better world". Find out more about Trip.com Group here: group.trip.com. Follow us on: X , Facebook , LinkedIn , and YouTube.

top_news.title: Noida
top_news.summary: BusinessWire India Noida (Uttar Pradesh) [India], October 13: Aadinath Ur Homes, a Noida-based real estate consultancy and advisory firm with more than two decades of experience in the region, led by CEO & Director Gaurav Jain, said Noida's commercial real estate market is entering a new phase of growth, supported by infrastructure expansion, improving regional connectivity, rising corporate demand and the commencement of commercial flight operations at Noida International Airport in June 2026. The operationalisation of Noida International Airport, along with continued infrastructure development across the Noida-Greater Noida and Yamuna Expressway corridors, is adding a new dimension to the region's commercial growth outlook. This comes amid sustained momentum in India's office market. According to CBRE's India Office Figures Q3 2026, India's office sector recorded approximately 21.0 million sq. ft. of absorption in Q3 2026, taking January-September absorption to a record 66.4 million sq. ft., up 8% year-on-year. Delhi-NCR, Bengaluru and Hyderabad together accounted for 69% of quarterly leasing activity. Infrastructure and connectivity reshape Noida's commercial landscape Connectivity is becoming an increasingly important consideration for businesses evaluating office and commercial locations. Noida benefits from established road infrastructure, metro connectivity and links with Delhi, Greater Noida and other NCR markets. The Noida-Greater Noida Expressway and Yamuna Expressway have supported the development of new commercial, institutional, residential and logistics corridors. The infrastructure-led expansion is also contributing to the emergence of newer commercial locations beyond Noida's traditional business districts. As development extends towards Greater Noida and the Yamuna Expressway corridor, businesses and investors are increasingly evaluating locations based on accessibility, workplace quality, proximity to residential catchments, supporting infrastructure and long-term development potential. The growth of commercial infrastructure is also supporting the emergence of new business hubs across Noida and the wider region. Areas along major expressways and established commercial corridors are attracting office developments, retail destinations, hospitality projects and mixed-use developments, creating broader ecosystems for businesses and consumers. Noida International Airport strengthens regional connectivity A major milestone for the region in 2026 has been the commencement of commercial operations at Noida International Airport. Noida International Airport commenced commercial flight operations on June 15, 2026, with IndiGo operating the first commercial flight. The airport had earlier received its aerodrome licence from the Directorate General of Civil Aviation. The first phase of the airport has been designed to serve 12 million passengers annually, while the master plan provides for phased expansion to more than 70 million passengers annually. The airport is also developing an integrated cargo and logistics ecosystem. Its cargo facilities have an initial handling capacity of 200,000 metric tonnes annually, with plans to scale capacity substantially. The cargo infrastructure is designed to support e-commerce, freight forwarding and logistics activity across North India. The airport's operationalisation adds another layer to the economic infrastructure of Noida, Greater Noida and the Yamuna Expressway region, with potential implications for aviation-linked businesses, logistics, hospitality, retail and commercial development. The development is also expected to strengthen the broader regional ecosystem by improving access to domestic and international markets and supporting the growth of allied commercial activity. Corporate expansion continues to support office demand The broader Indian office market is also being supported by expansion from domestic and global occupiers. CBRE reported that Global Capability Centres accounted for approximately 41% of India's office space take-up in Q3 2026, while GCC leasing during the first nine months of 2026 reached a record approximately 28 million sq. ft. Flexible workspace operators accounted for 24% of Q3 leasing, followed by BFSI companies at 22% and technology companies at 15%. Independent research from Colliers also points to continued strength in Delhi-NCR. The region recorded 8.3 million sq. ft. of Grade A office leasing during January-September 2026, representing a 17% year-on-year increase, while Q3 leasing reached 3.3 million sq. ft. For Noida, these broader trends are relevant as the city continues to attract technology companies, financial services firms, startups, healthcare organisations, educational institutions, multinational corporations and professional services businesses. The resulting commercial ecosystem is increasingly diversified, spanning office spaces, retail destinations, mixed-use developments, serviced apartments and other business-oriented formats. For businesses, access to quality commercial spaces, connectivity to residential catchments and proximity to major transportation networks are becoming increasingly important factors in location decisions. This is supporting demand across strategically located commercial micro-markets. Aadinath Ur Homes' commercial market presence Aadinath Ur Homes has advisory and sales involvement across a range of commercial developments in Noida and Greater Noida, including Bhutani Cyberthum in Sector 140A, Noida; Bhutani Astrathum in Greater Noida West; Bhutani City Centre 32 in Sector 32, Noida; and Spectrum Metro in Sector 75, Noida. These developments represent a mix of office spaces, retail destinations, mixed-use SOHO formats and serviced apartments, reflecting the changing nature of commercial real estate demand across Noida and the wider NCR market. From an advisory perspective, commercial opportunities are evaluated on factors including location, connectivity, project status, developer credentials, surrounding development, market demand and leasing potential. Evolving commercial corridors create new opportunities Noida's commercial growth is increasingly extending beyond its established business districts. Infrastructure-led development along major expressways and connecting corridors is creating opportunities for new office, retail, hospitality and mixed-use destinations. From an investment perspective, infrastructure can play an important role in shaping the long-term potential of a real estate market. Improved connectivity, employment generation, commercial activity and supporting social infrastructure can collectively influence the attractiveness of emerging locations. The increasing integration of commercial developments with retail, hospitality, entertainment and lifestyle offerings is also creating more comprehensive business destinations rather than standalone office or retail clusters. As businesses continue to evaluate locations based on connectivity, accessibility and operational efficiency, commercial corridors with strong infrastructure linkages are likely to remain areas of interest. Looking ahead Noida's next phase of commercial growth is being shaped by the convergence of infrastructure development, corporate expansion and regional connectivity. The operationalisation of Noida International Airport represents a significant addition to the region's infrastructure network, while its developing passenger and cargo ecosystem could support further economic activity across Noida, Greater Noida and the Yamuna Expressway corridor. At the same time, the latest 2026 data from CBRE and Colliers points to continued demand for quality office space across India and Delhi-NCR. The record 66.4 million sq. ft. of office absorption across India during January-September 2026 and 8.3 million sq. ft. of Grade A leasing in Delhi-NCR during the same period reflect continued occupier activity. For investors and occupiers, the evolving market reinforces the importance of evaluating individual projects on fundamentals rather than relying solely on broader market trends. Factors such as location, connectivity, surrounding development, tenant or consumer demand, developer credentials, project status and the potential evolution of the micro-market remain important considerations. With infrastructure, connectivity and business activity continuing to develop, Noida is positioned to remain an important commercial destination within the wider Delhi-NCR economic ecosystem. top_news.title: 60 Thai Employers Recognized at the HR Asia Best Companies to Work for in Asia 2026 Amid Evolving Workplace Trends
top_news.summary: BANGKOK, Oct. 13, 2026 /PRNewswire/ -- On 25 September 2026, HR Asia has officially announced the 60 winning organizations of the HR Asia Best Companies to Work for in Asia 2026 (Thailand Edition). Selected from a highly competitive pool of participants, these companies have demonstrated exceptional resilience, innovative workplace policies, and a deep commitment to employee well-being, setting the gold standard for human resources in the region. Congratulations to the winners of the 2026 Thailand HR Asia Best Companies to Work for in Asia The 2026 awards, organised by Business Media International are underpinned by the comprehensive Total Engagement Assessment Model (TEAM) survey, which polled 11,305 employees across 323 participating organizations to gauge their workplace sentiment. The data reveals a rapidly evolving Thai HR landscape defined by a stark contrast between thriving ground-level camaraderie and the pressing challenges of structural burnout. Navigating Current HR Trends in Thailand The Thai corporate sector is currently experiencing a unique dichotomy. According to the 2026 TEAM survey insights, the most significant strength across organizations is peer-to-peer support, with a record-high score of 4.65 (out of 5) for employees willingly assisting colleagues. Furthermore, employees are finding profound meaning in their roles (4.52) and highly rate their companies' commitments to Environmental, Social, and Governance (ESG) initiatives (4.50), as well as robust skill development policies (4.50). However, the broader HR landscape in Thailand is grappling with signs of systemic fatigue. Top-down rigidity and workload pressures remain significant hurdles. Survey metrics indicate that employees often feel excluded from structural decision-making (scoring a survey-low 3.93) and are experiencing low energy levels and exhaustion at work (3.94). There is also a clear demand for greater workplace flexibility over rigid processes (4.07). The winners of 2026 have successfully navigated these exact challenges. They have managed to bridge the gap between executive policy-making and ground-level employee involvement, fostering environments that not only encourage upskilling but actively work to mitigate burnout through empathetic leadership, purpose-driven cultures, and peer collaboration. The Strategic Advantage of the HR Asia Award In a Thai labor market where top talent increasingly prioritizes mental well-being, flexibility, and corporate ethics over traditional compensation alone, winning the HR Asia Best Companies to Work for in Asia award provides a critical competitive advantage. For the winning companies, this recognition serves as validated, data-backed proof of their employer brand strength. It establishes them as organizations that do not merely pay lip service to employee engagement, but actively cultivate a supportive, inclusive (4.42), and sustainable (4.48) workplace. This verifiable distinction significantly enhances their ability to attract premium talent, improve employee retention, and maintain a highly motivated workforce capable of driving long-term business success. By proving their commitment to ESG, upskilling, and meaningful work, these companies are well-positioned to mitigate the industry-wide risks of burnout and turnover. As the Thai workforce continues to demand more holistic support and structural flexibility, the 2026 winners stand as a testament to the power of putting people first. They have proven that empowering employees and fostering peer support are not just HR buzzwords, but essential pillars of a modern, resilient business strategy. "This year's data highlights a critical turning point for the Thai HR landscape," said Datuk William Ng, Chairman, HR Asia Best Companies to Work for in Asia. "While it is inspiring to see such strong peer-to-peer collaboration and alignment with corporate purpose, the underlying signs of employee exhaustion cannot be ignored. The winning companies this year have set themselves apart not just by recognizing this dichotomy, but by actively implementing empathetic, flexible structures that empower their people and bridge the gap between leadership and the ground-level workforce." The 2026 winners serve as a blueprint for business adaptability, proving that an organization's most valuable asset remains its people. By investing in continuous upskilling, flexible working arrangements, and inclusive, purpose-driven work environments, these companies not only secure the talent necessary to sustain Thailand's economic momentum but also set the standard for corporate excellence across the region. The award covers several markets across the region including mainland China, Cambodia, Hong Kong, Indonesia, India, Japan, Korea, Macau, Malaysia, Philippines, Singapore, Taiwan, Thailand, United Arab Emirates, and Vietnam, making this the largest recognition program and survey in the region for employee engagement. articles.title: Malta Tourism Authority and Trip.com Group Sign Strategic Cooperation Memorandum of Understanding to Promote Malta as a Global Destination
articles.summary: VALLETTA, Malta, Oct. 13, 2026 /PRNewswire/ -- On the sidelines of the 2026 WTTC Global Summit held in Malta, Carlo Micallef, CEO of the Malta Tourism Authority, met with Edison Chen, Vice President of Trip.com Group, for talks on China-Malta tourism cooperation. Witnessed by Jo Etienne Abela, Malta's Minister for Tourism, the Malta Tourism Authority and Trip.com Group formally signed the 2026-2029 Strategic Cooperation Memorandum of Understanding. Malta Tourism Authority and Trip.com Group sign a Strategic Cooperation Memorandum of Understanding to promote Malta as a global destination over the next three years. DOI (Malta) The signing of the Strategic Cooperation MOU marks a further deepening of the strategic partnership between the Malta Tourism Authority and Trip.com Group. Over the next three years, the two parties will carry out in-depth cooperation in destination promotion, tourism product diversification and sustainable tourism. (From left to right) Carlo Micallef, CEO of the Malta Tourism Authority, together with Jo Etienne Abela, Malta's Minister for Tourism, met with Edison Chen, Vice President of Trip.com Group, for talks on China-Malta tourism cooperation. Trip.com Group "Malta is committed to diversifying its source markets, and China is the most important emerging market in our strategic plans," said CarloMicallef, CEO of the Malta Tourism Authority. "Our partnership with Trip.com Group will help us reach high-value travellers in China and around the world more precisely, and showcase Malta's unique appeal as a premium Mediterranean tourism destination." Edison Chen, Vice President of Trip.com Group, said, "Malta is a vibrant destination, offering a wealth of cultural and premium experiences, and excellent connectivity. Our data shows a 60% growth in inbound travel bookings to Malta, underscoring its growing appeal among global travellers. By combining Trip.com Group's global reach and platform technology with Malta's unique offerings, we are excited to further boost tourism in Malta, inspiring more travellers from Asia and around the world to discover its beauty." Malta Accelerates Its Push into the Asian Market Malta is actively expanding into the Asian market, with plans to raise the share of arrivals from outside the EU to 40% within the next decade. Carlo Micallef, CEO of the Malta Tourism Authority, said that Malta is advancing tourism cooperation discussions with China and several other Asian countries. Although Schengen visa requirements remain a short-term challenge, the market potential is immense. Trip.com Group's platform coverage advantages across the world's major source markets, together with its leading big-data and AI-supported capabilities, will help Malta enhance its brand influence as a premium tourism destination. With a large presence in Asia, Europe and across global markets, Trip.com Group is highly strategically aligned with the Malta Tourism Authority's market diversification strategy. The 2026 WTTC Global Summit was held from 7 to 9 October at the Mediterranean Conference Centre in Valletta, bringing together tourism industry CEOs and senior government leaders from more than 100 countries. The signing is one of the significant cooperation outcomes achieved during the Summit. Over the next three years, the two parties will leverage the technological capabilities and data insights of Trip.com Group's global platforms, combined with the Malta Tourism Authority's in-depth understanding and integration of local tourism resources, to continuously optimise promotional strategies and position Malta as a highly attractive Mediterranean tourism destination for global travellers. About Trip.com Group Trip.com Group is a global travel service provider comprising of Trip.com, Ctrip, Skyscanner, and Qunar. Across its platforms, Trip.com Group helps travellers around the world make informed and cost-effective bookings for travel products and services and enables partners to connect their offerings with users through the aggregation of travel-related content and resources, and an advanced transaction platform consisting of apps, websites and 24/7 customer service centres. Founded in 1999 and listed on NASDAQ in 2003 and HKEX in 2021, Trip.com Group is on the mission "to pursue the perfect trip for a better world". Find out more about Trip.com Group here: group.trip.com. Follow us on: X , Facebook , LinkedIn , and YouTube.

articles.title: Noida
articles.summary: BusinessWire India Noida (Uttar Pradesh) [India], October 13: Aadinath Ur Homes, a Noida-based real estate consultancy and advisory firm with more than two decades of experience in the region, led by CEO & Director Gaurav Jain, said Noida's commercial real estate market is entering a new phase of growth, supported by infrastructure expansion, improving regional connectivity, rising corporate demand and the commencement of commercial flight operations at Noida International Airport in June 2026. The operationalisation of Noida International Airport, along with continued infrastructure development across the Noida-Greater Noida and Yamuna Expressway corridors, is adding a new dimension to the region's commercial growth outlook. This comes amid sustained momentum in India's office market. According to CBRE's India Office Figures Q3 2026, India's office sector recorded approximately 21.0 million sq. ft. of absorption in Q3 2026, taking January-September absorption to a record 66.4 million sq. ft., up 8% year-on-year. Delhi-NCR, Bengaluru and Hyderabad together accounted for 69% of quarterly leasing activity. Infrastructure and connectivity reshape Noida's commercial landscape Connectivity is becoming an increasingly important consideration for businesses evaluating office and commercial locations. Noida benefits from established road infrastructure, metro connectivity and links with Delhi, Greater Noida and other NCR markets. The Noida-Greater Noida Expressway and Yamuna Expressway have supported the development of new commercial, institutional, residential and logistics corridors. The infrastructure-led expansion is also contributing to the emergence of newer commercial locations beyond Noida's traditional business districts. As development extends towards Greater Noida and the Yamuna Expressway corridor, businesses and investors are increasingly evaluating locations based on accessibility, workplace quality, proximity to residential catchments, supporting infrastructure and long-term development potential. The growth of commercial infrastructure is also supporting the emergence of new business hubs across Noida and the wider region. Areas along major expressways and established commercial corridors are attracting office developments, retail destinations, hospitality projects and mixed-use developments, creating broader ecosystems for businesses and consumers. Noida International Airport strengthens regional connectivity A major milestone for the region in 2026 has been the commencement of commercial operations at Noida International Airport. Noida International Airport commenced commercial flight operations on June 15, 2026, with IndiGo operating the first commercial flight. The airport had earlier received its aerodrome licence from the Directorate General of Civil Aviation. The first phase of the airport has been designed to serve 12 million passengers annually, while the master plan provides for phased expansion to more than 70 million passengers annually. The airport is also developing an integrated cargo and logistics ecosystem. Its cargo facilities have an initial handling capacity of 200,000 metric tonnes annually, with plans to scale capacity substantially. The cargo infrastructure is designed to support e-commerce, freight forwarding and logistics activity across North India. The airport's operationalisation adds another layer to the economic infrastructure of Noida, Greater Noida and the Yamuna Expressway region, with potential implications for aviation-linked businesses, logistics, hospitality, retail and commercial development. The development is also expected to strengthen the broader regional ecosystem by improving access to domestic and international markets and supporting the growth of allied commercial activity. Corporate expansion continues to support office demand The broader Indian office market is also being supported by expansion from domestic and global occupiers. CBRE reported that Global Capability Centres accounted for approximately 41% of India's office space take-up in Q3 2026, while GCC leasing during the first nine months of 2026 reached a record approximately 28 million sq. ft. Flexible workspace operators accounted for 24% of Q3 leasing, followed by BFSI companies at 22% and technology companies at 15%. Independent research from Colliers also points to continued strength in Delhi-NCR. The region recorded 8.3 million sq. ft. of Grade A office leasing during January-September 2026, representing a 17% year-on-year increase, while Q3 leasing reached 3.3 million sq. ft. For Noida, these broader trends are relevant as the city continues to attract technology companies, financial services firms, startups, healthcare organisations, educational institutions, multinational corporations and professional services businesses. The resulting commercial ecosystem is increasingly diversified, spanning office spaces, retail destinations, mixed-use developments, serviced apartments and other business-oriented formats. For businesses, access to quality commercial spaces, connectivity to residential catchments and proximity to major transportation networks are becoming increasingly important factors in location decisions. This is supporting demand across strategically located commercial micro-markets. Aadinath Ur Homes' commercial market presence Aadinath Ur Homes has advisory and sales involvement across a range of commercial developments in Noida and Greater Noida, including Bhutani Cyberthum in Sector 140A, Noida; Bhutani Astrathum in Greater Noida West; Bhutani City Centre 32 in Sector 32, Noida; and Spectrum Metro in Sector 75, Noida. These developments represent a mix of office spaces, retail destinations, mixed-use SOHO formats and serviced apartments, reflecting the changing nature of commercial real estate demand across Noida and the wider NCR market. From an advisory perspective, commercial opportunities are evaluated on factors including location, connectivity, project status, developer credentials, surrounding development, market demand and leasing potential. Evolving commercial corridors create new opportunities Noida's commercial growth is increasingly extending beyond its established business districts. Infrastructure-led development along major expressways and connecting corridors is creating opportunities for new office, retail, hospitality and mixed-use destinations. From an investment perspective, infrastructure can play an important role in shaping the long-term potential of a real estate market. Improved connectivity, employment generation, commercial activity and supporting social infrastructure can collectively influence the attractiveness of emerging locations. The increasing integration of commercial developments with retail, hospitality, entertainment and lifestyle offerings is also creating more comprehensive business destinations rather than standalone office or retail clusters. As businesses continue to evaluate locations based on connectivity, accessibility and operational efficiency, commercial corridors with strong infrastructure linkages are likely to remain areas of interest. Looking ahead Noida's next phase of commercial growth is being shaped by the convergence of infrastructure development, corporate expansion and regional connectivity. The operationalisation of Noida International Airport represents a significant addition to the region's infrastructure network, while its developing passenger and cargo ecosystem could support further economic activity across Noida, Greater Noida and the Yamuna Expressway corridor. At the same time, the latest 2026 data from CBRE and Colliers points to continued demand for quality office space across India and Delhi-NCR. The record 66.4 million sq. ft. of office absorption across India during January-September 2026 and 8.3 million sq. ft. of Grade A leasing in Delhi-NCR during the same period reflect continued occupier activity. For investors and occupiers, the evolving market reinforces the importance of evaluating individual projects on fundamentals rather than relying solely on broader market trends. Factors such as location, connectivity, surrounding development, tenant or consumer demand, developer credentials, project status and the potential evolution of the micro-market remain important considerations. With infrastructure, connectivity and business activity continuing to develop, Noida is positioned to remain an important commercial destination within the wider Delhi-NCR economic ecosystem. articles.title: 60 Thai Employers Recognized at the HR Asia Best Companies to Work for in Asia 2026 Amid Evolving Workplace Trends
articles.summary: BANGKOK, Oct. 13, 2026 /PRNewswire/ -- On 25 September 2026, HR Asia has officially announced the 60 winning organizations of the HR Asia Best Companies to Work for in Asia 2026 (Thailand Edition). Selected from a highly competitive pool of participants, these companies have demonstrated exceptional resilience, innovative workplace policies, and a deep commitment to employee well-being, setting the gold standard for human resources in the region. Congratulations to the winners of the 2026 Thailand HR Asia Best Companies to Work for in Asia The 2026 awards, organised by Business Media International are underpinned by the comprehensive Total Engagement Assessment Model (TEAM) survey, which polled 11,305 employees across 323 participating organizations to gauge their workplace sentiment. The data reveals a rapidly evolving Thai HR landscape defined by a stark contrast between thriving ground-level camaraderie and the pressing challenges of structural burnout. Navigating Current HR Trends in Thailand The Thai corporate sector is currently experiencing a unique dichotomy. According to the 2026 TEAM survey insights, the most significant strength across organizations is peer-to-peer support, with a record-high score of 4.65 (out of 5) for employees willingly assisting colleagues. Furthermore, employees are finding profound meaning in their roles (4.52) and highly rate their companies' commitments to Environmental, Social, and Governance (ESG) initiatives (4.50), as well as robust skill development policies (4.50). However, the broader HR landscape in Thailand is grappling with signs of systemic fatigue. Top-down rigidity and workload pressures remain significant hurdles. Survey metrics indicate that employees often feel excluded from structural decision-making (scoring a survey-low 3.93) and are experiencing low energy levels and exhaustion at work (3.94). There is also a clear demand for greater workplace flexibility over rigid processes (4.07). The winners of 2026 have successfully navigated these exact challenges. They have managed to bridge the gap between executive policy-making and ground-level employee involvement, fostering environments that not only encourage upskilling but actively work to mitigate burnout through empathetic leadership, purpose-driven cultures, and peer collaboration. The Strategic Advantage of the HR Asia Award In a Thai labor market where top talent increasingly prioritizes mental well-being, flexibility, and corporate ethics over traditional compensation alone, winning the HR Asia Best Companies to Work for in Asia award provides a critical competitive advantage. For the winning companies, this recognition serves as validated, data-backed proof of their employer brand strength. It establishes them as organizations that do not merely pay lip service to employee engagement, but actively cultivate a supportive, inclusive (4.42), and sustainable (4.48) workplace. This verifiable distinction significantly enhances their ability to attract premium talent, improve employee retention, and maintain a highly motivated workforce capable of driving long-term business success. By proving their commitment to ESG, upskilling, and meaningful work, these companies are well-positioned to mitigate the industry-wide risks of burnout and turnover. As the Thai workforce continues to demand more holistic support and structural flexibility, the 2026 winners stand as a testament to the power of putting people first. They have proven that empowering employees and fostering peer support are not just HR buzzwords, but essential pillars of a modern, resilient business strategy. "This year's data highlights a critical turning point for the Thai HR landscape," said Datuk William Ng, Chairman, HR Asia Best Companies to Work for in Asia. "While it is inspiring to see such strong peer-to-peer collaboration and alignment with corporate purpose, the underlying signs of employee exhaustion cannot be ignored. The winning companies this year have set themselves apart not just by recognizing this dichotomy, but by actively implementing empathetic, flexible structures that empower their people and bridge the gap between leadership and the ground-level workforce." The 2026 winners serve as a blueprint for business adaptability, proving that an organization's most valuable asset remains its people. By investing in continuous upskilling, flexible working arrangements, and inclusive, purpose-driven work environments, these companies not only secure the talent necessary to sustain Thailand's economic momentum but also set the standard for corporate excellence across the region. The award covers several markets across the region including mainland China, Cambodia, Hong Kong, Indonesia, India, Japan, Korea, Macau, Malaysia, Philippines, Singapore, Taiwan, Thailand, United Arab Emirates, and Vietnam, making this the largest recognition program and survey in the region for employee engagement.
